# Questions of interest
Is there a difference in mean systolic blood pressure between current cigarette smokers and non-current smokers among U.S. adults aged 18 and older?

# Link to download: 
```{r}
install.packages("nhanesA", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(nhanesA)

bpx <- nhanes("BPX_J")
smq <- nhanes("SMQ_J")


```

# DATA DESCRIPTION

## Who recorded the data and how?

The data come from the 2017–2018 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), run by the CDC’s National Center for Health Statistics.

Participants were randomly selected to represent the U.S. population. They answered health questions in a home interview and had physical measurements taken by trained staff at a mobile exam center.

We combined three NHANES files (blood pressure, smoking, and demographics), linked by participant ID.

**Data source:** https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/

## Key Variables

- **Systolic blood pressure (`BPXSY1`–`BPXSY3`)**: Up to three readings (mmHg), taken after the participant sat quietly for 5 minutes. We average them into one value per person, our outcome.

- **Smoking status (`SMQ020`)**: "Have you smoked at least 100 cigarettes in your life?" (Yes/No). This defines our two groups, ever-smokers and never-smokers.

- **Age (`RIDAGEYR`)**: Used to keep only adults aged 20 and older.

## What Does a Row Represent?

One adult aged 20+ who took part in NHANES 2017–2018, with their average systolic blood pressure and smoking status.

## What Is the Population?

Civilian U.S. adults aged 20 and older living in households (excluding the military, prisons, and nursing homes).

Because NHANES over-samples some groups and we do not use its sampling weights, our sample may not perfectly reflect this population.


# An outline of a graph related to your question of interest.
## Graph1: side-to-side boxplot
x-axis: ever-smoke VS never smoke(SMQ020)
y-axis: systolic blood pressure/mmHg (BPXSY1-3)
purpose: compare the mean, spread, skew and outliers of blood pressure between the two groups

## Graph2: null distribution histogram
x-axis: difference in sample mean between ever-smoke and never smoke
y-axis: frequency
purpose: gain p-value by using a resampling hypothesis test to determine whether there was a significant difference in average blood pressure between the two groups.

## Graph3: histogram of the bootstrap 
x-axis: difference in resample mean between ever-smoke and never smoke
y-axis: frequency
purpose: obtain a confidence interval for the difference in means, giving the range of plausible values.


# The type of inference method
We plan to use inference on the difference of two population means to investigate whether there is a statistically significant difference in mean systolic blood pressure between current smokers and never-smokers.

We will use a two-sample t-test to compare the mean systolic blood pressure of the two groups and construct a 95% confidence interval for the difference in population means.
